title: Gift Wrap Roll

drivers.name: Price increase (3.4%)
drivers.evidence: Price rose to $5.72 from $5.53; past promotions with similar or larger discounts had noise-adjusted lift of x1.0, suggesting limited impact. No evidence of demand elasticity.

drivers.name: Supplier delivery warning
drivers.evidence: Planner note indicates possible supply constraint, reducing available units and likely lowering sales. No past data on delivery issues, so effect is uncertain but plausible.

adjustment.analysis: The target week has no events, but a 3.4% price increase to $5.72. Past promotions show a median lift of x1.15, but noise-adjusted effect is x1.0. The price increase is modest and not seen in prior promotions. Supplier delivery warning introduces supply risk, lowering demand. No recent promotion or seasonal ramp in the baseline. The classical model suggests x1.0, but the price increase and supply concern justify a downward adjustment. Evidence is thin, so shrink toward 1.0. The baseline’s uncertainty is already calibrated.

brief:
PRODUCT: Gift Wrap Roll | category Seasonal | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-22 (6 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 5.72 (+3.4% vs regular price 5.53)
  planner notes: Supplier warns of a short delivery

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 3.1 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 10.7 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 9.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-95% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
